turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? Is there something specific that’s been troubling you lately?
turns.patient_response: Yeah… I came in because I just feel restless all the time. Like I’ve got a motor running inside me, and I can’t shut it off. If I have to sit still—like at church, or here at the clinic, or even at home—I start feeling trapped, and I’ve got to get up or do something.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient reports feeling restless all the time, describes an internal 'motor,' and says being required to sit still makes them feel trapped and compelled to get up or do something.

turns.doctor_question: Does this feeling of restlessness happen all the time, or only in certain situations or places?
turns.patient_response: It’s pretty much all day, not just one place. It shows up at church, here at the clinic, even at home. If I’m supposed to sit still, I start feeling trapped, like I’ve got to get up and do something.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient reports feeling trapped and needing to get up or do something whenever expected to sit still, occurring throughout the day across church, clinic, and home.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel this restlessness, does it come along with feeling anxious or worried about things?
turns.patient_response: I don’t really know. I mean, I don’t think I’m sitting there worrying about something specific most of the time. It’s more like my body just won’t settle down.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient says they are not usually worrying about something specific, denying persistent excessive worry in this context.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel this restlessness, do you also feel inner tension or an urge to move, even if you’re not anxious or worried about anything?

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any actual movements, like rocking, pacing, or fidgeting, when you feel that inner restlessness?

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient describes repeated leg bouncing, finger tapping, and twisting objects in their hands while trying to sit still.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever been on any medications that might have caused this restlessness, especially ones used for mental health, stomach issues, or nausea?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve been on anything like that, at least not that I know of. I haven’t noticed it starting from a medicine or anything.

turns.doctor_question: Is the restlessness something you feel even when you're not sitting still—like when you're standing around or in situations where you don't have to stay quiet or inactive?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it’s kind of there all the time. Even if I’m just standing around and don’t have to be quiet, I still feel like there’s a motor going inside me. It’s worse when I have to sit still, like at church or here at the clinic, but even at home I end up needing to get up or do something.

turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. It’s like I’ve got a motor running inside me most of the day. Even at home, when nobody’s making me sit still, I still end up needing to get up or do something. If I have to stay seated, like at church or here, I start feeling trapped.
